title: Comment on "Andreev Reflection to Probe Momentum-Dependent Spin Polarization in Altermagnet CrSb"
authors: Igor I. Mazin, Maxim Khodas, Boris Nadgorny
abstract: Zhang et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016701 (2026)] report momentum-dependent spin polarization in the altermagnet CrSb from point-contact Andreev reflection along the (0001), (-1-120), and (10-10) directions. We show that the Andreev spin polarization they claim to measure is forbidden by symmetry: it vanishes identically in the diffusive regime for all directions in CrSb, and in the ballistic regime for two of the three orientations measured. It is allowed only along one direction, where the calculated band structure gives ~50%. The large, nearly isotropic values reported follow from an incorrect definition of ballistic Andreev spin polarization that evaluates the spin asymmetry at fixed three-dimensional momentum; the Andreev selection rule is local only in the momentum component parallel to the interface. Moreover, the ballistic regime is not demonstrated, and the fitting procedure is flawed.
summary: This theoretical work critiques experimental claims of observing momentum-dependent spin polarization in CrSb using Andreev reflection. By applying symmetry arguments, the authors show that the measured ASP is forbidden by symmetry in the diffusive regime and for most measured directions in the ballistic regime. This suggests the original measurements may stem from flawed definitions or experimental artifacts rather than genuine physical effects.
main_problem: The paper challenges claims regarding the observation of momentum-dependent spin polarization (Andreev Spin Polarization, ASP) in the altermagnet CrSb using point-contact Andreev reflection (PCAR).
main_result: The authors demonstrate that the claimed ASP is forbidden by symmetry in the diffusive regime for all measured directions and is forbidden in the ballistic regime for two of the three measured orientations.
method: The analysis uses symmetry constraints and theoretical derivations for both the diffusive and ballistic regimes of Andreev reflection to calculate the expected ASP.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the altermagnet CrSb, analyzing spin transport properties across a point contact interface.
key_observables: Andreev Spin Polarization (ASP) measured via point-contact Andreev reflection (PCAR).
important_parameters: Crystallographic orientations ((0001), (-1-120), (10-10)), diffusive vs. ballistic regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on symmetry properties (e.g., C2^perp||Mn) and the theoretical framework of Andreev reflection in magnetic materials.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by analyzing the theoretical constraints imposed by symmetry on the ASP in both the diffusive and ballistic limits, contrasting these findings with the original claims.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of symmetry principles to interpret complex transport measurements in magnetic topological materials is highly relevant for understanding spin-charge coupling in condensed matter systems.
